newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: West Australia state to introduce gold royalty.
newsitem.headline: West Australia state to introduce gold royalty.

text.p: A royalty on gold production will be phased in next year, Western Australian Premier Richard Court said on Thursday.

Announcing the state's 1997/98 budget, he said the royalty would start on January 1 at "a low rate", with an exemption for the first 1,000 ounces of production from each project. "We will be consulting with the industry in the forthcoming months to determine the final framework of the royalty," Court said.
The Premier did not specify the royalty rate, but referred to an initial rate of 1.25 percent and a final rate of 2.5 percent when he first floated the idea last month.

Australian gold producers said ahead of the budget announcement that Western Australia would lose A$500 million a year in gold production and investment in the industry would be cut by A$200 million if the state government introduced a 2.5 percent gold royalty.

The Association of Mining and Exploration Companies (AMEC), reporting results of a survey of nine mines across the state with forecast production life of 260 tonnes of gold, said the survey also indicated there would be an average reduction in mine lives of one year.

The industry also has said that while the proposed royalty would raise about A$70 million-A$90 million a year, this would be offset by reduced production, payroll tax, stamp duties and other taxes and charges paid by gold producers and their suppliers.

The University of Western Australia said a 2.5 percent royalty would reduce gold production by the same amount, reduce gross domestic product by A$370 million and produce an associated income loss for the state of A$250 million, AMEC said.

Queensland has a 2.75 percent gross royalty, New South Wales has a net smelter levy of four percent, equal to about a two percent gross royalty, and the Northern Territory has an 18 percent net profit royalty.
